q1_issues.issue: The scale symbol "increase" occurs nowhere in the text, contrary to the rule that a Measure's scale is the surface dimension (stated adjective, else the dimension noun); and Measure states a value, not the increment that "rose a tenth of a percentage point" denotes.

"a tenth of a percentage point" is silently arithmetic-reduced to the magnitude 0.1, whereas the instruction set keeps fractional amounts as a Fraction term and elsewhere forbids the translator doing the arithmetic itself.

(Most level sk_rate_1 unemployment_rate) mis-fills the superlative slots: the scale must be the lemmatized adjective ("highest" -> high), and the thing ranked is the 6.1% level, not the rate itself, so the atom reads "the rate is the most level among unemployment rates".
"since July 1994" is dropped entirely - no Time / TimeAtLeast / Start atom anywhere records the window the superlative claim is made relative to.

q2_gaps: a measured increment or decrement of a quantity over time ("rose a tenth of a percentage point") - Measure encodes a value and MoreBy a comparative gap, but no form covers a delta predicated of a change event
the endpoint of such a change ("rose ... to 6.1%") - motion-result Goal is defined for paths, not for a resulting numeric value, and Measure on the entity loses the link to the event
a superlative restricted to a time window ("the highest level since July 1994") - Most has only <scale> <entity> <class> and no slot for the comparison window
a fractional magnitude of a unit ("a tenth of a percentage point") - Fraction is defined for partitives over a definite set, not for a quantity of a measurement unit
notes: The unemployment_rate compound (genus emitted, noun modifier not exposed) and Patient on the non-volitional intransitive subject of "rose" are both correct. Everything numeric in the sentence is either invented (the "increase" scale), reduced by hand, or dropped ("since July 1994").
